x_failures: Hippocratic 'duly proportioned... compounding, power, and quantity' is credited to Galen; the wording is accurate and appears on the cited p.76, so this is misattribution of the author, not invention.
y_failures: Table traits such as 'Virtuous, cheerful', 'Quick-tempered, daring' and 'Sluggish, pale' are cited to Corpus Christi MS 441 p.146, which has only the desires/can-do formulas. Most of these traits are on the Trinity MS p.62, and 'cheerful' appears on neither page. Sennert p.115 also does not discuss disease as dyscrasia.
reason: Both answers are mostly well grounded, but Y answers the temperament part of the question more directly, with an element–humor–temperament table and examples of disease (phrenitis, sorrow), and cites more relevant primary pages (Aristotle, Sennert on concoction, Ibn al-Nafis). Y's misattributions are mild because most of the traits appear on another page it cites, so it still serves the reader better than X.
